findings: Species identity is correct: the plate depicts Black Skimmer, Rynchops niger, family Laridae, with the diagnostic black-and-white plumage, extremely long red-and-black bill, projecting lower mandible, long pointed wings, short red-orange legs, and webbed feet.

The printed measurements are correct: length 40–50 cm (15.8–19.7 in), weight 265–365 g (9.3–12.9 oz), and wingspan 109–115 cm (42.9–45.3 in) match the live All About Birds account. Animal Diversity Web independently confirms the length and mass ranges and gives a compatible average wingspan of 112 cm.

Every visible title, taxonomy line, measurement, habitat line, behavior line, field-mark bullet, ruler label, schematic disclaimer, and palette label is legible and matches the proposed facts without material spelling, number, duplication, omission, substitution, or word-order errors.

Both depicted heads were checked independently. In the primary specimen and detached head study, the mandibles share a coherent base, the lower mandible projects conspicuously beyond the upper by a degree comparable to the clearest side-profile reference, and neither upper mandible looks reversed, co-terminal, truncated, or inconsistently proportioned.

The primary specimen has one head, one bill, two folded wings, two legs with webbed feet, and one short tail. Its sleek, low-slung proportions, white forehead and underparts, black cap and upperparts, red-orange proximal bill with black distal portion, dark eye, and pointed folded wings are consistent with the references and live descriptions.

The isolated wing and head-and-bill renderings read clearly as detached supplementary studies rather than extra birds or parts attached to the primary specimen. The wing has plausible pointed flight feathers and a white trailing edge; the head study preserves the vertical pupil and diagnostic unequal mandibles.

The body-length ruler is internally consistent: 40 cm / 15.8 in is at the bottom, 50 cm / 19.7 in is at the top, values increase upward, there are exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks forming five proportional segments, and the plate explicitly labels it “SCHEMATIC – NOT TO SCALE.”

The composition is orderly and readable, with the primary specimen dominant and the supplementary studies clearly separated. Lower-page elements are somewhat dense but do not overlap or impair interpretation.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, observation locality, or other local-observation detail appears.
